candidates.snippet: Lech Wałęsa is consistently described across 11 model source lists as influential for: Led the Solidarity movement in Poland, contributing to the fall of Communism; Co-founded Solidarity, the Soviet bloc's first independent trade union, and served as President of Poland; Lech Walesa changed normative and intellectual frameworks through texts and teachings embedded in schools, law, or public discourse; Reshaped state power through war, diplomacy, or institutional reform with effects beyond their own generation; Labor leader; co-founded Solidarity; instrumental in ending communism in Poland; Leader of the Solidarity movement in Poland, which played a key role in the collapse of communism in Eastern Europe; Polish statesman, dissident, and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, who co-founded and led Solidarity, the first independent trade union in the Warsaw Pact; Founded Solidarity, the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc, triggering the fall of communism.
